title: I have called you friends (John 15:9–17)
hookLine: greater love has no one than this

cards: It's late on the last night, and the supper is nearly over.

Jesus is talking to eleven friends, a few hours before his arrest, and he says a line that would end up carved on war memorials and on plaques for soldiers, firefighters and nurses: greater love hath no man than this.
People reach for it when someone has given their life for others. But at the table it was said about friendship. And the sentence right after it is just as surprising.

teach.h: GREATER LOVE: A LIFE FOR FRIENDS.
teach.b: Here's the line in full, in the King James Bible: "Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends." For his friends. That word is the key.
Jesus has just repeated the commandment he gave earlier that same evening: love one another, as I have loved you. Then he names what they are to him.
"Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends."

teach.h: A SERVANT ISN'T TOLD; A FRIEND IS.
teach.b: A servant follows orders and isn't told the reasons. A friend is let in on the plan. That's the difference, Jesus says: all things that I have heard of my Father I have made known unto you.
The Greek word is philoi, friends, from the same family as philos, loved one. In the Hebrew Bible, very few people get called God's friend. Abraham is one, in Isaiah and in Chronicles.
Of Moses, Exodus says God spoke with him face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. So this is a big word to hand to eleven ordinary men, fishermen and a tax collector among them.

teach.h: YE HAVE NOT CHOSEN ME; I CHOSE YOU.
teach.b: Then one more turn: "Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you." In those days students usually picked their teacher. Here the teacher did the picking.
Christians hear two things in this passage, and they hold them together.
One is comfort: being chosen, let in, called friend. The other is the cost: a friendship measured by a life laid down. Many Christians see that measure fulfilled the next day, at the cross.

how: Many Christians speak of Jesus as a friend in prayer and in hymns, and John 15:13 is read at many memorial services for people who died serving others.

games.q: you're the teacher. your students have followed you for years. tonight, what do you call them?
games.why: "Henceforth I call you not servants... but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard of my Father I have made known unto you."

practice: Think of a friend, and of something they need that you could actually do: picking up their kid, proofreading their resume, returning the dish, listening to the long story again.
Picture doing it the way a friend does, not like a servant ticking a box. Then think of one person who has done that for you, and let yourself be grateful; if you pray, give thanks for them by name.

wordCard.voice: Friends. Not servants who follow orders without knowing why, but what Jesus calls his own: friends let in on the plan.
